scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Marley's definitive death and Scrooge's unrelenting commercial pragmatism following his partner's demise.
required_beats: Marley dies and Scrooge signs the burial register
Scrooge solemnises the funeral by conducting business

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes Scrooge's callousness and misanthropy by showing him reject his nephew's warmth and charitable appeals.
required_beats: Scrooge works in the cold counting-house while his clerk freezes
Scrooge's nephew arrives with Christmas greetings and invites Scrooge to dinner
Scrooge rebuffs his nephew and threatens to discharge the clerk
Two gentlemen visit seeking donations for the destitute
Scrooge refuses to give anything to the poor and resumes working alone

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Contrasts Scrooge's cold stinginess with the festive spirit shared across the wider city from the grandest to the humblest homes.
required_beats: The Lord Mayor orders his household to keep Christmas
A poor tailor prepares his pudding while his wife and baby fetch beef

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Concludes the workday by emphasizing Scrooge's hostility toward holiday cheer and his grudging accommodation of his clerk.
required_beats: Scrooge threatens a carol-singing boy at the keyhole and scares him off
Scrooge prepares to close up and extracts a promise of early arrival from the clerk
Scrooge shuts down the office and departs

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To contrast Scrooge's cold bitterness with the clerk's spontaneous holiday joy and vitality.
required_beats: The clerk celebrates his release by sliding down the icy gutter at Cornhill.
The clerk runs home toward Camden Town.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To establish Scrooge's austere, isolated routine on Christmas Eve.
required_beats: Scrooge eats his solitary evening meal at his usual melancholy tavern.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To shatter Scrooge's mundane reality by confronting him with the horrific supernatural arrival of his deceased partner.
required_beats: Scrooge arrives at his gloomy chambers and is startled by Marley's face appearing on the door knocker.
Scrooge retreats inside, checks his rooms for intruders, and locks himself in before the hearth.
Unexplained ringing bells give way to sounds of heavy chains dragging upward from the cellar.
Marley's Ghost passes into the room and identifies itself to a skeptical Scrooge.
The Ghost removes its bandage, letting its jaw drop, and terrifies Scrooge onto his knees.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To deliver Marley's warning of impending supernatural visitation and leave Scrooge shaken by a glimpse of the spirit world.
required_beats: Marley's Ghost demonstrates the weight of the chain he forged in life, frightening a trembling Scrooge.
The Ghost rebinds its jaw and glides backward to the open window.
The Ghost departs into the mist to join an exterior wailing chorus of phantoms.
Scrooge checks the locked door and collapses exhausted into bed.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To introduce the first supernatural guide and initiate Scrooge's journey of reckoning with his past.

char_scrooge.goal: to lie awake until the hour was passed

required_beats: Scrooge wakes at midnight and waits anxiously in his bed as the clock strikes one.
A sudden flash of light reveals the Ghost of Christmas Past at his bed curtains.
Scrooge questions the spirit about its identity and its purpose in visiting him.
The Ghost takes Scrooge by the arm and leads him toward the window.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To breach Scrooge's emotional defenses by confronting him with the painful isolation of his childhood.
required_beats: Scrooge and the Spirit materialize on a familiar country road from Scrooge's youth.
Scrooge recognizes passing boys celebrating the holidays and feels a swell of emotion.
The Spirit leads Scrooge into his old schoolhouse to find his solitary younger self reading by the fire.
Weeping at the sight of his lonely former self, Scrooge expresses regret.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To link Scrooge's childhood grief to his recent harsh treatment of a street caroler.
required_beats: A boy sings a Christmas carol at the door.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To transition Scrooge to the next phase of his remembered past.
required_beats: The Ghost of Christmas Past gestures to summon another Christmas.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Breaks young Scrooge's growing isolation and despair through the loving arrival of his sister.
required_beats: Young Scrooge paces the schoolroom in despair as time passes.
Fan runs into the room and embraces him warmly.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Explains why Scrooge is suddenly permitted to return home from his long exile.
required_beats: Fan asks their father if Scrooge may return home.
Their softened father agrees to the request and sends Fan in a coach to bring Scrooge back.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Concludes Scrooge's school days with formal farewells as he is carried off to family life.
required_beats: Fan leads young Scrooge out of the schoolroom.
The schoolmaster receives them in the best parlour and offers hospitality.
The children bid the schoolmaster goodbye and depart together in the chaise.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes the loss of the primary loving bond from Scrooge's youth.
required_beats: Fan passes away.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Reminds Scrooge of the generosity and warmth of his early master, confronting him with how easily an employer can bring happiness to others.
required_beats: The Ghost leads Scrooge to Fezziwig's warehouse, where the young apprentices prepare the room for a Christmas Eve party.
A lively ball takes place with music, dancing, and festive celebration led by Mr. and Mrs. Fezziwig.
As the party ends, Fezziwig bids everyone goodnight, and the young apprentices praise his goodness while Scrooge looks on.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Forces Scrooge to witness the moment his growing greed destroyed his chance at love and domestic happiness.
required_beats: Scrooge watches his younger self sit with Belle as she confronts him about his changed priorities.
Belle releases young Scrooge from their engagement and parts from him forever.
An anguished Scrooge begs the Spirit to show him no more, but the Spirit compels him to continue watching.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Breaks Scrooge with the vision of the warm family life he lost, driving him to forcefully extinguish the Spirit.
required_beats: The Ghost shows Scrooge Belle surrounded by a joyful, boisterous family greeting her husband with Christmas gifts.
Belle's husband tells her he saw Scrooge sitting entirely alone in his office.
Overcome with grief, Scrooge wrestles with the Ghost and forces the extinguisher-cap down over its head.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Concludes the journey with the first Spirit and returns Scrooge to his bed in exhausted slumber.
required_beats: Scrooge finds himself back in his bedroom, collapses into bed, and immediately falls asleep.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Introduces the Ghost of Christmas Present and establishes Scrooge's willingness to be taught.
required_beats: Scrooge awakes at one o'clock and follows a glowing light into his adjoining room.
The Ghost of Christmas Present reveals himself and identifies his lineage of elder brothers.
Scrooge submits voluntarily to the Spirit's guidance and takes hold of his robe.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Demonstrates the communal joy and charity of Christmas morning among common folk and clarifies the Spirit's benevolent nature.
required_beats: Scrooge and the Spirit witness the energetic bustle of people clearing snow and crowding grocers' shops.
The Spirit uses his torch to bless the dinners carried to the bakers and quell street disputes.
Scrooge questions the Spirit on Sabbath restrictions and receives a rebuke against attributing bigotry to the Spirits.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Establishes the warmth, poverty, and playful affection of the Cratchit family as they prepare for dinner.
required_beats: The Spirit brings Scrooge to Bob Cratchit's dwelling and blesses the threshold with his torch.
The Cratchit children and their mother hurriedly prepare dinner.
Martha arrives, briefly hides in play, and embraces Bob as he returns carrying Tiny Tim.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Confronts Scrooge with Tiny Tim's precarious mortality and forces him to reckon with the human impact of his callous beliefs.
required_beats: The Cratchits joyfully share their modest meal of goose and pudding.
Scrooge inquires about Tiny Tim's fate, and the Spirit uses Scrooge's own cruel words to warn of the boy's death.
Bob leads a toast to Scrooge, which Mrs. Cratchit and the children reluctantly drink.
The family spends the evening talking and listening to Tiny Tim sing before the Spirit bears Scrooge away.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To show Scrooge the widespread merriment and cheerful spirit spreading through ordinary people in the city streets.
required_beats: Scrooge and the Ghost of Christmas Present move through the city streets.
Passersby, including a group of girls and a laughing lamplighter, display cheerful holiday spirits around the Spirit.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reveal to Scrooge that warmth, harmony, and Christmas joy flourish even among impoverished laborers in bleak isolation.
required_beats: Scrooge and the Ghost travel across a bleak moor and enter a miner's hut.
An old miner and his assembled family celebrate Christmas by singing together.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate that the Christmas spirit reaches even the most remote and desolate outposts.
required_beats: The Ghost conveys Scrooge across the sea to a solitary lighthouse.
Two lightkeepers toast to Christmas over their grog.
The elder lightkeeper sings a sturdy song.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To underscore that solitary men far from home remain united in Christmas observance across dark waters.
required_beats: Scrooge and the Ghost fly over the sea and board a ship.
They observe the ship's officers and watchmen keeping their stations.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To awaken Scrooge's longing for human warmth, family affection, and festive fellowship.
required_beats: Scrooge watches Fred and his companions laughing about Scrooge's rejection of Christmas and wealth.
Fred insists he feels only pity for his uncle and leads the guests in music and parlor games.
Scrooge softens under the music and eagerly tries to participate in the guessing games from afar.
The party reveals the subject of their riddle to be Scrooge, and Fred toasts him with mulled wine.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To transition Scrooge away from the warmth of the holiday gatherings as his time with the spirit wanes.
required_beats: The gathering at Fred's dissolves as the Spirit and Scrooge resume their journey.
Scrooge and the Spirit visit and depart from a festive children's party.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To confront Scrooge with the societal ruin caused by neglect and bring the second Spirit's visitation to an ominous close.
required_beats: As the night draws near its end, the Ghost reveals two wretched children clinging beneath its robes.
Scrooge recoils in horror, and the Spirit warns him of Ignorance and Want.
The clock strikes midnight, and the Ghost of Christmas Present vanishes.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To introduce the final, ominous spirit and establish Scrooge's terrified resolve to learn from it.
required_beats: A solemn, draped Phantom advances through the darkness toward Scrooge.
Scrooge falls to his knees and questions the silent Spirit about its identity and purpose.
Scrooge professes his readiness to accompany the Phantom, urging it to lead the way.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate the complete indifference and callous amusement of Scrooge's business peers upon hearing of a prominent man's death.

char_scrooge.goal: to lie awake until the hour was passed
treasure up every word he heard, and everything he saw; and especially to observe the shadow of himself

required_beats: Scrooge and the Phantom arrive at the 'Change to observe a knot of businessmen.
The businessmen casually discuss the death of an acquaintance and joke about only attending the funeral for a free meal.
The Phantom shows Scrooge two more acquaintances who dismiss the death with brief, indifferent remarks.
Scrooge observes intently, resolving to find the lesson and look out for his future self.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reveal the utter degradation and predation surrounding the deceased man, whose very deathbed was stripped by his servants.
required_beats: The Phantom brings Scrooge to Old Joe's pawnshop in a squalid part of town.
The charwoman, Mrs. Dilber, and the undertaker's man arrive together to pawn stolen goods taken from the dead man's quarters.
Old Joe evaluates and buys the stolen wares of the undertaker's man and Mrs. Dilber.
The charwoman reveals she stripped the bed-curtains and burial shirt directly from the lonely corpse, and Old Joe pays them out.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To confront Scrooge directly with the solitary, uncared-for corpse of the unlamented man.

char_scrooge.goal: treasure up every word he heard, and everything he saw; and especially to observe the shadow of himself
see someone who feels emotion at the dead man's death

required_beats: The Phantom transports Scrooge to a dark, bare bedroom containing a covered corpse.
The Phantom points repeatedly toward the deceased's face, but Scrooge cannot bring himself to uncover it.
Scrooge pleads with the Phantom to show him anyone who feels emotion over this person's death.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reveal that the only emotion provoked by the man's death is pure relief from his desperate debtors.
required_beats: Caroline anxiously greets her husband upon his arrival home.
Her husband reveals that their ruthless creditor has died.
Caroline expresses deep gratitude and relief at the news, though she asks forgiveness for feeling thankful.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To pivot the vision from unfeeling detachment to genuine mourning by showing Scrooge's need for proof of tenderness connected with death.

char_scrooge.goal: see someone who feels emotion at the dead man's death
see tenderness connected with a death

required_beats: Scrooge begs the Spirit to show him tenderness associated with death.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To transition Scrooge toward the home where true grief resides.
required_beats: The Ghost conveys Scrooge through the city streets toward Bob Cratchit's dwelling.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reveal the devastating emotional contrast of Tiny Tim's death and show how profoundly a tender soul is mourned.
required_beats: The quiet Cratchit family sits together as Peter reads until Bob arrives home.
Bob comforts his family and speaks of his visit to Tiny Tim's burial ground.
Overwhelmed by grief, Bob retreats upstairs to weep beside Tiny Tim's body.
Bob returns to the hearth and recounts meeting Scrooge's nephew, who offered heartfelt sympathy and assistance.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To resolve the Cratchits' grief into enduring mutual love and solidarity.
required_beats: The family gathers around Bob to share kisses and a comforting handshake.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Forces Scrooge to confront his own impending, unmourned demise and drives him to absolute despair and repentance.
required_beats: The Spirit leads Scrooge past his former business haunts to an overgrown churchyard.
Scrooge approaches the grave indicated by the Spirit and reads his own name on the stone.
Scrooge drops to the ground and clutches the Spirit's hand in desperate pleading, only to be rebuffed.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Shows Scrooge waking to find he has been granted a second chance at life, immediately channeling his ecstatic relief into generosity.

char_scrooge.goal: see tenderness connected with a death
send the turkey to Bob Cratchit's

required_beats: The Phantom dwindles into Scrooge's bedpost, leaving Scrooge to realize he has returned alive to his chambers.
Scrooge dresses in joyous haste and learns from a boy outside that it is Christmas Day.
Scrooge hires the boy to fetch the prize turkey to send anonymously to Bob Cratchit.
Scrooge greets the delivery, pays the poulterer and the boy, and prepares himself for the day in high spirits.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Demonstrates Scrooge actively repairing his past harshness by offering lavish charity to the gentleman he previously turned away.
required_beats: Scrooge walks the streets in his finest clothes and encounters the portly gentleman.
Scrooge takes the gentleman's hands and whispers a large charitable donation.
The stunned gentleman gratefully shakes Scrooge's hand and agrees to visit him.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: Marks Scrooge's spiritual reconciliation with his community and faith on Christmas Day.
required_beats: Scrooge attends church service and walks among his fellow citizens.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To reconcile Scrooge with his surviving family by fulfilling Fred's Christmas invitation.
required_beats: Scrooge arrives at his nephew's house and asks to be let in.
Scrooge enters the dining room and asks Fred if he may join dinner.
Fred joyfully welcomes Scrooge into the gathering.
The rest of the guests arrive to join the celebration.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To demonstrate Scrooge's genuine transformation through practical benevolence toward his clerk.
required_beats: Scrooge waits in his office as Bob Cratchit arrives late for work.
Scrooge pretends to reprimand Bob for his tardiness.
Scrooge surprises Bob by wishing him a merry Christmas, raising his salary, and pledging aid to his family.

scene_cards.dramatic_function: To resolve the story by confirming Scrooge's enduring redemption and bond with Tiny Tim.
required_beats: Scrooge lives out his life as a generous friend, master, and second father to Tiny Tim.
